messages:
eva: FYI from ACME support ticket #8247 — their internal service endpoint `payments.acme.internal` suddenly started returning NXDOMAIN for pods in their prod cluster after the hosted zone merge yesterday. Customer reports 500s from app because env resolves to public LB.
samir: Thanks, digging in. Which cluster/VPC?
eva: cluster=prod-us-east-1a, k8s namespace=payments, VPC=vpc-0a1b2c3d, account=acme-prod-123
samir: Got it. First quick sanity checks: can pods resolve DNS at all? Any node-local or iptables redirects?
eva: Customer ran a quick `kubectl exec` into a pod and did `dig payments.acme.internal +short` -> returned nothing (no answer). Host `curl` to the internal fqdn times out.
mike: Can you paste the `dig` output (including header)? need to see NXDOMAIN vs SERVFAIL. Also want NodeLocal DNS IP — node-local caches often at 169.254.20.10 in our clusters.
eva: Paste from customer (trimmed):
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> payments.acme.internal @169.254.20.10 +tcp
;; global options: +cmd
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0
;; SERVER: 169.254.20.10#53(169.254.20.10)
;; Query time: 2 msec
```

mike: OK NXDOMAIN from node-local. Now test upstream -- run `dig payments.acme.internal @10.100.0.2` (account resolver IP) if possible. Also check `kubectl get configmap node-local-dns -n kube-system` for `hosts`/stubDomains.
ashley: I also want to confirm whether that private hosted zone was merged/changed yesterday. If a private hosted zone in acme-core got merged into a shared zone or copied to another account, VPC associations could have been lost. Can we get Route53 HostedZoneId?
eva: Customer provides hosted zone IDs: Z1PA2BCDE34FGH (old), Z9XY8WVU7TSRQ (merged). They said they merged using internal tool at 2024-06-21 22:40 UTC.
jane: If the shared hosted zone (Z9XY...) is not associated with vpc-0a1b2c3d, Route53 resolver will return NXDOMAIN for private names from that VPC. Can you run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name` and `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z9XY8WVU7TSRQ` in acme-prod account and share VPC associations?
samir: Customer ran `get-hosted-zone` and shows `VPCs: []` (empty) for Z9XY8WVU7TSRQ. That seems to be the issue — merge created a new hosted zone and associations weren't migrated.
mike: Good catch. Two follow-ups: 1) Why did node-local return NXDOMAIN instead of forwarding to another chain? Because node-local forwards to account resolver which uses Route53 private hosted zones; if the hosted zone isn't associated, NXDOMAIN is expected. 2) Why are some external requests still hitting public LB (causing TLS mismatch/500)? Because app fallback logic hits public DNS if internal fails.
easily: Proposed immediate mitigation for customer: add VPC association back to Z9XY8WVU7TSRQ (AssociateVPCWithHostedZone). This requires account owner perms and cross-account association if the zone is in shared account. If we can't change DNS immediately, temp workaround: add stubDomain entry in CoreDNS to forward `acme.internal` to the resolver IP of the account that still has the hosted zone (if available).
jane: Note: cross-account association via `AssociateVPCWithHostedZone` requires that the hosted zone owner authorize the association (`ChangeResourceRecordSets` not required). If hosted zone is in a different account, they must use `create-vpc-association-authorization` first.
samir: Repro steps we used:
1) from a pod: `dig payments.acme.internal @169.254.20.10 +tcp` -> NXDOMAIN
2) from a bastion in same VPC: `dig payments.acme.internal @11.22.33.44` (the acme-core resolver) -> ANSWER: A 10.42.3.5 (internal LB)
3) `kubectl exec` curl to IP works, curl to FQDN fails due to NXDOMAIN
4) Route53 `get-hosted-zone` for merged zone -> shows no VPCs

mike: Can we get the timeline of the merge and who executed it? Might need to revert or re-run migration that preserves associations. Also check CloudTrail for `AssociateVPCWithHostedZone`/`DisassociateVPCFromHostedZone` calls around 2024-06-21 22:30-23:00 UTC.
eva: Customer says their infra tool did a zone merge and removed old zone Z1PA2... then created Z9XY... and intended to migrate association but missed it. They don't see `DisassociateVPCFromHostedZone` in CloudTrail.
ashley: If there's no disassociate call, another possibility is that the tool created a new hosted zone and the VPC association never existed for the new zone. So we need to add it. But since it's cross-account, they need hosted-zone owner to authorize.
samir: I'm proposing we do this: 1) instruct customer to open a ticket with zone-owner (acme-core) to run `aws route53 create-vpc-association-authorization --hosted-zone-id Z9XY... --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c3d` then the customer account runs `associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone`. Provide exact CLI snippets.
easily: Also recommend they add a short term CoreDNS stubDomain: edit configmap coredns in kube-system and add:
```
stubDomains:
  "acme.internal": ["11.22.33.44"]
```
This will forward queries for `acme.internal` directly to acme-core resolver until hosted zone is associated. Reminder: change rollouts may need kube-dns restart.
jane: One more thing: node-local cache TTL might have cached NXDOMAIN — ask customer to `kubectl delete pod -l k8s-app=node-local-dns -n kube-system` or restart the daemonset to clear cache; or wait for TTL. Also check `journalctl -u node-local-dns` for errors.
mike: Safety checks before association: confirm there are no overlapping private hosted zones (same name) in different accounts — Route53 will prefer the one in the account with association; overlapping private zones can cause split-horizon weirdness. Run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones` across accounts to ensure uniqueness.
eva: Customer agrees to contact acme-core to get association authorization. They've also applied the coredns stubDomain as stopgap and restarted node-local. Reports now `dig payments.acme.internal @169.254.20.10 +tcp` -> returns `10.42.3.5`.
samir: Great. After the association completes, confirm removal of stubDomain. Also validate app SNI/cert: once FQDN resolves internally to internal LB, TLS cert should chain correctly — ask them to `openssl s_client -connect payments.acme.internal:443 -servername payments.acme.internal` to confirm cert CN/SANs.
ashley: Filing a short internal postmortem: root cause = hosted zone merge workflow created new private hosted zone without migrating VPC associations (human/tooling gap). Impact = internal svc FQDN NXDOMAIN, fallback to public LB causing errors and TLS mismatch. Action items: 1) patch merge tool to migrate associations or require authorization step, 2) add pre-merge validation checks to detect unmatched VPC associations, 3) docs for runbook with stubDomain temporary workaround.
sre-oncall-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2024-4829 (linked to support case #8247).
eva: Closing loop with customer now. They will coordinate acme-core to authorize and we will verify once association done. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
